title: CrlChecker docstring claims Ok(()) for not-covered IDP scope, but code returns OutOfScope
description: In pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, the CrlChecker struct-level rustdoc (lines 68-80) claims that check_revocation returns Ok(()) in two cases: (1) not revoked, and (2) not covered by IDP scope flags. It explicitly says 'These two outcomes are indistinguishable from the caller's perspective.' However, the actual code (lines 620-636) returns Err(Error::OutOfScope(...)) for IDP scope mismatches, which IS distinguishable. The rustdoc is stale — it predates the OutOfScope variant addition. What goes wrong: a caller reading the struct-level doc believes Ok(()) may mean 'not covered' and writes defensive code to handle that ambiguity, when in fact OutOfScope is now a distinct error. Conversely, a caller who only reads the struct doc may not realize they need to handle OutOfScope in their error matching. Location: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs lines 66-80.
